title: Priority Decoder & Initiative Stewardship Canvas
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, lightweight artifact we call the 'Priority Decoder' and an associated Initiative Stewardship Canvas to translate company-level OKRs into ranked, resourced, and timeboxed initiatives across teams. The Decoder should reduce ambiguity about why an initiative exists, who owns tradeoffs, and what decision SLA applies when conflicts arise.

Scope: Deliver a one-page canvas template, a triage rubric (quantitative + qualitative scoring), steward assignment rules, a short runbook for resolving interlock conflicts, and a Confluence template and sample filled canvases for three pilot initiatives (Console, Runtime, and Dedicated).

Acceptance criteria: 1) For each company objective, produce a ranked list of initiatives (<=5) with assigned steward and owner; 2) Each initiative entry includes success metric, estimated effort bucket, top 3 dependencies, and a risk/mitigation line; 3) The triage rubric yields repeatable scores (documented thresholds) and is validated by at least two PM, two Eng, and one Design reviewer; 4) Conflict runbook defines decision SLA (3 business days for medium-priority, 5 business days for low) and escalation path to ELT; 5) Confluence template published and linked from roadmap hub; 6) Pilot run completed with stakeholder survey showing >=70% clarity improvement vs current state.

Deliverables: Priority Decoder rubric (sheet + examples), Initiative Stewardship Canvas (Confluence template + PNG), pilot cohort report, updated roadmap hub link, and PR to product playbook.

Stakeholders: PM (owner): Aisha Patel; Engineering leads: Priya Singh and Marcus Lee; Design partner: Nora Kim; GTM liaison: Olivia Park; Executive sponsor: CTO (Elena Ramos).

Success metrics: alignment score (survey-based) improved by >=30 percentage points in pilot, reduction in cross-team decision latency by 40%, and decreased rework measured as fewer than 2 mid-cycle priority swaps per initiative in pilot cohort.

Risks: Overly prescriptive rubric that fails to scale to hundreds of initiatives, lack of engagement from engineering leads, and edge cases where customer escalations override rubric. Mitigations include preserving an exceptions channel with logged rationale and a quarterly rubric review.

Rollout plan: 1) Draft canvas (2 weeks) 2) Internal review and iterate with two pod leads (1 week) 3) Pilot on 3 initiatives during Cycle 2026-W06 (4 weeks) 4) Revise and publish organization-wide (2 weeks).
